author: nicodevs
body:
## Goal

Add a start screen before each level and a countdown timer that ends the game when it runs out.

## What changed

- Each level now opens with a full-screen overlay showing a 🚀, a "Level X" title, and a Start button. Clicking Start fades the overlay out quickly (200ms) and the level begins once the fade finishes.
- A countdown in seconds sits above the board. It begins the moment the start overlay finishes fading out, and counts down once per second. The number turns red at 5 seconds or less.
- Reaching 0 ends the game and shows the Game Over screen, reusing the same path as running out of HP.
- The timer freezes in place (it is not reset) when the level is won or lost mid-countdown, so the remaining time stays visible on the Victory and Game Over screens.
- Timer length scales with the level: `(level + 1) * 10` seconds, so level 1 is 20s, level 2 is 30s, level 3 is 40s, and so on.
- Retry and Continue both re-show the start overlay for the level being played, giving each attempt a fresh timer.

The countdown lives in a small `useTimer` composable (start resets and runs the count, stop freezes it, expiry fires a callback once). `useGame` now exposes `endGame` so a timeout can trigger game over the same way HP depletion does.

## Screenshots

Start overlay shown at the beginning of a level:

![start overlay](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79ba2953-68c8-4f4c-bf4a-7e736a05ca04)

Countdown above the board during play:

![game timer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bae4cab-4a02-4263-ab40-7925e9f94dda)

## Migrations or schema changes

None.

## How to test

1. `npm run dev` and click PLAY.
2. Confirm the Level 1 start overlay appears with the 🚀, title, and Start button, and the timer behind it reads 20.
3. Click Start and confirm the overlay fades out fast and the countdown begins ticking down.
4. Let the timer reach 0 and confirm the game ends and the timer stays frozen at 0.
5. Start a new level, win or lose it before the timer expires, and confirm the timer freezes at its current value.
6. Advance to Level 2 and confirm its overlay appears with a 30 second timer.

body: ## Problem Opening the Git Manager on a multi-repo **workspace** project rendered the sub-repo dropdown correctly but **also toasted "Not a git repository"** every time. ## Cause On open, the section data fetch fires immediately with no `repoPath` (the `selectedRepo` hasn't resolved yet), so the git status request targets the **non-git browse-only workspace root** and fails `Not a git repository`. `fetchWorkspaceRepos` resolves a tick later and the fetch re-runs against a real sub-repo — but the first failure had already toasted. ## Fix Track workspace detection in a ref and suppress that single benign root-race error: no `repoPath` + `Not a git repository` while detection is still pending or has confirmed a workspace. A genuinely broken **non-workspace** project still surfaces the error — once detection settles as non-workspace, a single *guarded* re-fetch re-surfaces it. The guard ensures no redundant fetch in the common non-workspace-OK path, preserving existing call-count expectations. ## Tests - Added the missing `fetchWorkspaceRepos` api mock — a pre-existing gap (from the git-manager commit) that had broken the **entire** GitManagerModal suite at import (130 tests). - Positive regression: workspace project → no `Not a git repository` toast. - Negative control: real non-workspace broken repo → the error still toasts. Dashboard typecheck + lint clean; my 2 new tests pass and no previously-passing test regressed (8 unrelated pre-existing failures remain, untouched by this change). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Workspace tasks now return aggregated, repo-prefixed diff results for both detailed diffs and file-diff listings, including consistent file/stats aggregation across sub-repositories. * **Bug Fixes** * Prevented an initial, harmless “Not a git repository” message from being shown during early workspace detection; genuine errors still display the standard error toast. * Improved workspace detection and retry behavior so the UI loads the correct repo context after project switching. * Updated the Task Changes UI to handle workspace tasks without incorrectly showing the “No worktree available” state. * **Tests** * Added/expanded coverage for workspace diff aggregation and workspace-related UI/error behaviors.

> 🤖 This PR was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

## Summary

Phase-1 go/no-go measurement for the warp foundation (issue #823). Wires a real `:kuilt-websocket` Netty/OkHttp fabric under `WarpNode` and measures duplicate-execution rate vs spike predictions.

**Measured results:**
- 3-node hub-spoke fleet (60 tasks): **22.1% dup-rate** — within the ≤35% budget; comfortably above the D-GOSSIP@0%churn 0% prediction (the extra dup overhead comes from ring disagreement across the hub-spoke topology gap, as expected).
- 2-node fleet / failover (20 tasks): **0.0% dup-rate** — both nodes converge, 0 dups.

**Bugs fixed** (found only by this real-IO test):
- `recordResult`/`removeFromQueue` had a racy read-compute-apply: concurrent executor coroutines read the same base CRDT state, each calling `ORMap.put`/`ORSet.remove`, minting **duplicate causal dots**. On `piece()` merge, the causal tombstoning logic silently dropped entries sharing a dot — results disappeared with no error. Fix: hold `WarpNode.lock` across the entire read → compute → `quilter.apply` sequence.
- `QuilterConfig` defaults (`antiEntropyInterval=1min`, `fullStateRetryInterval=30s`) exceed the 30s test window. Shortened to 2s/3s so a missed delta heals in-test.

## Test plan

- [ ] `./gradlew :kuilt-warp:jvmTest` — both WarpNodeWebSocketTest tests pass in ~7s
- [ ] `./gradlew :kuilt-warp:detektAll` — clean

## #1175 — fail-safe guard
Ephemeral runner her job sonrası exit-0 yapar → `Restart=always` re-register için **doğru**. Ama config/run KALICI fail ederse (bozuk token, ağ, repo erişimi) runner anında çıkar ve `RestartSec` ile hızlı re-register → GitHub token-API spam/rate-limit busyloop.

Fix: `StartLimitIntervalSec=300` + `StartLimitBurst=5` → 5dk'da >5 restart olursa servis durur (failed), normal job-başına-tek-restart akışında asla tetiklenmez. `RestartSec` 5→10.

> Not: code-review #1175 önerisi (`Restart=on-failure`) **yanlıştı** — ephemeral exit-0=başarı, her job sonrası restart İSTENİR; rate-limiting doğru çözüm.

## Summary

This PR improves the reliability of the Wallstop PR Comments extension when collecting and rendering suggested changes from GitHub PR review comments.

## User-facing changes

- Suggested changes are now sourced in a safer order: GitHub API markdown suggestions first, then GitHub web PR files parsing, then optional browser HTML fallback.
- Suggested diffs found via web/browser parsing are now only trusted when they come from GitHub automated comment data, reducing false positives from user-authored text.
- Copy output now reports where attached suggested diffs came from, making results easier to understand.
- Adds optional browser fallback support via the user/global setting `wallstopPrComments.browserWebSuggestionsCommand`.
- Improves handling of external bot comments (such as Cursor/Bugbot) so unavailable fixes are clearly labeled instead of being inferred incorrectly.
- Improves embedded location parsing and matching logic for comments so file/line attribution is more consistent.

## Quality and test coverage

- Adds a new extension test suite file and significantly expands parser, web suggestion, GitHub client, and renderer tests.
- Updates extension internals and type contracts to support provenance/confidence metadata and more robust ID matching.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes copy/paste output and web HTML/cookie/browser enrichment for PR comments; mistakes could attach wrong suggested diffs or mis-attribute locations, but parsing is intentionally conservative and browser fallback is opt-in.
> 
> **Overview**
> Strengthens **Wallstop PR Comments** when copying PR review threads: suggested fixes are gathered in a fixed trust order (API `suggestion` fences, then GitHub PR `/files` HTML, then an opt-in browser HTML provider), and copy warnings name **where** attached web diffs came from (`githubWebAutomatedDiff`, `browserDomAutomatedDiff`, etc.).
> 
> Adds application-scoped **`wallstopPrComments.browserWebSuggestionsCommand`** so a VS Code command can supply logged-in PR files HTML; only **global** config is honored. **`getWebSuggestedDiffs`** tries unauthenticated fetch first, then sanitized cookie, then browser fallback when enabled; web parsing accepts only **`automatedComment.suggestion.diffEntries`**, with tighter ID matching (numeric/string `databaseId`, discussion URLs) and rejection of forged JSON in comment bodies.
> 
> **Cursor/Bugbot** handling is tightened: exact bot logins via **`botAuthors`**, embedded `LOCATIONS` may override file/line for trusted bots (with mismatch guards), prose cleanup strips bot chrome, and external fixes are labeled **unavailable** instead of inferring diffs from `diffHunk`. Copilot web-only cases use the same conservative unavailable rules. Types and render output gain **source/confidence** metadata and **cross-path** `Suggested change (<path>):` labels. Documentation and tests cover the new contracts end-to-end.

body:
Closes #3081

## What changed
- Updated Stripe registration checkout creation to charge the next scheduled installment amount when a registration selected the installment plan, instead of always charging the full form total.
- Persisted installment progress on the registration after Stripe payment succeeds, including paid installment count, remaining balance, and next due date.
- Added app UI messaging to show the amount due now and remaining installment schedule before checkout, plus the remaining schedule after a successful installment payment.
- Updated staff-facing registration payment labels to surface installment-in-progress state from stored registration data.

## Root Cause
The checkout flow stored the selected installment plan on the registration, but `createStripeRegistrationCheckout` ignored that stored plan and always recomputed Stripe charges from the full authoritative form total. The success-state UI and stored payment state also assumed every successful Stripe payment meant the registration was fully paid.

## Prevention / Learning
When the server stores an authoritative payment-plan snapshot, every downstream checkout, webhook, reminder, and confirmation path must derive amount due and remaining balance from that plan instead of assuming one full-balance payment.

## Regression Tests
- `functions/test/public-registration-submission.test.cjs` verifies installment registrations store the schedule, create checkout for the first installment amount, and persist installment-in-progress state after the Stripe webhook.
- `apps/app/src/pages/RegistrationDetail.test.tsx` verifies the registration page shows amount due now, remaining installment schedule before checkout, and remaining balance after successful installment payment.
- `tests/unit/app-parent-tools-service.test.js` verifies staff review labels reflect stored installment-in-progress payment state.

## Recurrence Risk
Medium. Payment flows span checkout creation, webhook mutation, and UI confirmation surfaces, so future changes can drift if one surface is updated without the others.

body:
## 0.12.0 — multi-agent honesty

Makes vibatchium's honest multi-agent boundary (a **per-agent daemon**) reachable from the CLI/MCP, fixes two concurrency bugs on the headline paths, and drops `fetch`'s needless ceremony. Grounded in a 6-dimension architecture audit and hardened by a fresh-eyes adversarial review (all confirmed findings remediated).

### Isolated-daemon front door (was SDK-only)
- `vb daemon start --isolated [--home][--runtime-dir][--idle-timeout]` and `vb mcp --isolated` spawn a private daemon on its own socket + HOME — separate profiles/config/state, own session budget, zero contact with the shared daemon.
- `vb daemon reap [--all]` sweeps abandoned ones (flock-serialized, atomically-written registry).
- The shared daemon stays the **default** — N private daemons would worsen the OOM blast radius, so isolation is opt-in (same UID = same trust domain; this bounds *blast radius*, not a security boundary).

### Concurrency / robustness
- **`go` auto-start** now creates the session under the registry `mutate_lock` (double-checked) — closes the Chrome `SingletonLock` create-collision two concurrent `go`-firsts on the implicit `default` session could hit.
- **`vb research`** bounds its pool to the session cap (slots recycle), degrades a slot-starved thread instead of aborting the whole run (a `SessionLimitError` used to propagate out of `fut.result()`), drops a redundant prewarm Chrome, and has a loop-level backstop for sibling `DaemonNotRunning`/timeouts.

### Sessionless fetch
- `vb fetch --no-cookies <url>` with no session does a true **anonymous GET** — coherent Chrome JA3/HTTP2 fingerprint, no cookies, no browser, no `vb start` (dispatcher routes fetch through `SESSIONLESS_FALLBACK_VERBS`; the handler decides). A cookie-wanting call with no session gets actionable guidance before the optional dep is required. New `--user-agent`.

### Resource governance (opt-in) + discoverability
- `VIBATCHIUM_SESSION_RAM_FLOOR_MB` refuses a cold launch below a memory floor (covers the default prewarm lane too); documented alongside the operator-level aggregate cgroup cap.
- uv-/editable-aware `vb update` and the missing-`curl_cffi` error (names the daemon's interpreter); `vb install` reports optional lanes informationally (a missing extra no longer fails the core verdict); `vb setup` warns when `vb` isn't on PATH; MCP server instructions gain a concurrency paragraph; README/AGENTS install lines surface the `[fetch]`/`[all]` extras.

### Also included
Lands the previously-uncommitted **0.11.1 `vb login`** (one-command headed login on a shared, headless-default box) — see the 0.11.1 CHANGELOG entry. It was never committed, so it ships here under 0.12.0.

### Verification
- +18 multi-agent unit/integration tests + 13 login tests; targeted regression green (1 pre-existing env-artifact failure, `test_wave8_bloat::test_clean_apply_json_requires_yes`, unrelated — fails identically with this work stashed); **21/21 real-scenario smoke** (real Chrome + `curl_cffi`: go-race, sessionless + session fetch, research recycle, isolated front door, RAM floor, reap orphan, two-agent parallelism); `ruff` clean.

author: ericgriffin
body:
Follow-up to #416, addressing a post-merge review finding.

## The finding (verified)

#416 made the OSTC nano download stop at the device's `0xFD 0xFD` end-of-profile marker instead of the over-declared length. A reviewer flagged — and I confirmed — that the code **comments and tests claimed a guarantee the code does not provide**: a notification dropped *before* the final marker (the same BLE bridge that loses bytes, #280) still delivers the final `FD FD` notification, so the buffer ends in the marker and is accepted as a complete (short) dive.

The downstream validation in `hw_ostc3_device_foreach` does **not** catch this:
- the end-marker check (`profile[length-2..length-1] == 0xFD 0xFD`) passes — the tail is intact;
- the length check (`array_uint24_le(profile+256)` vs `profile+9`) compares the **two declared length fields to each other** — both live in the intact early bytes, never the received count;
- the hwOS profile carries **no CRC**.

So such a dive is stored corrupt, and the original comment's claim that "a notification dropped mid profile still returns the error" was wrong.

## What this PR does

- **Corrects the `hw_ostc3_read_profile` comment** to state the limitation plainly (marker, not byte count, ends the profile; a pre-marker loss is accepted; downstream cannot catch it; retry narrows but cannot close the window; a less lossy link / BLE connection priority is the real mitigation).
- **Adds a native test** asserting and documenting the accepted-corrupt behavior (`lost-middle-with-FD-FD-tail is accepted as complete (known limitation)`), so the suite no longer implies the case is rejected.

**No behavior change** — comments and coverage only. Fork: `submersion-app/libdivecomputer@2b38c6e` on `submersion-patches`.

## Why not a byte-count guard (the reviewer's optional suggestion)

A received-vs-declared length cross-check would need a tolerance constant, and the firmware's over-declare amount is not yet known across dives/firmwares (one data point: ~18–21 bytes). body:
Closes #4703

## Summary

Normalize pasted HTML tables that use `colspan` in the first row so they still become parseable GFM tables instead of plain pipe text.

The failure is specific to the first row. MarkText already preprocesses pasted tables by turning the first row into header cells before Turndown runs, but it preserves the original `colspan` structure. When the first row contains a merged cell, the resulting Markdown table is no longer rectangular: the header row has fewer logical columns than the body rows. Turndown still emits pipe-table syntax, but `MarkdownToState` does not recognize it as a valid table, so the paste falls back to a plain paragraph.

This PR fixes that upstream of Turndown by expanding each first-row `colspan` into empty placeholder cells first. That keeps the table rectangular, so the existing HTML-to-Markdown and Markdown-to-state pipeline can keep doing its job without a special-case parser change.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking, fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking, adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (causes existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update

author: justin808
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3929. When the underlying RSC fetch for `getComponent` **rejects** (a transient renderer/network/deploy failure), the rejected promise was left in the provider's bounded payload cache, so every later same-key `getComponent` returned the cached rejection — an RSC route/component stayed wedged in its error state even after the backend recovered. Only an explicit `refetchComponent` or a full reload cleared it.

## Fix

`getComponent` now attaches a rejection handler (`evictPromiseIfRejected`) as the second argument to its `.then(...)`:

- **Re-throws** so React's Suspense machinery still observes the failure on the cached promise.
- **Evicts** the cached entry one macrotask later (`setTimeout(0)`, not `queueMicrotask`, so Suspense reads the rejection before the entry disappears).
- **Identity-guarded**: only deletes if the cache still holds *this* promise, so a newer same-key `getComponent`/`refetchComponent` started in that window is never evicted by the stale failure.
- **Preserves pins** (`deletePreservingPins`) so the existing `.finally()` still owns the matching `unpin` — mirroring the `restoreLastSuccessfulPromise` delete + deferred-unpin handoff.

Two-argument `.then(onFulfilled, onRejected)` is used over `.catch()` so an error thrown *inside* the success handler is not misread as a fetch rejection.

**Out of scope:** payloads that *resolve* with an `Error` value are intentionally left cached — whether those should also retry is a separate `getServerComponent` contract decision, noted in a code comment and tracked apart from #3929.

## Relationship to #4022

This supersedes the stale draft #4022, which patched the pre-LRU `getComponent`. Since #4022 was opened, #4097 rewrote `getComponent` (+328/−24) with the bounded-LRU cache, evicted-success markers, and in-flight pin latches, leaving #4022 unmergeable (`CONFLICTING`). This PR re-derives the small fix against current `main` and **ports #4022's test harness** (`RSCProbe`, the `0a/0b/0c` cases, and the real-timer eviction helper).

## Test plan

- `jest tests/imperativeRefetch.client.test.tsx` → 25/25 pass. New `0a/0b/0c` cover dedupe/caching, retry-after-rejection, and the stale-rejection-vs-newer-refetch guard. Verified `0b` **fails on `main` without the fix** (returns the cached rejection) and passes with it.
- Ran the RSCProvider-touching suites for regressions — `boundedCacheProvider`, `inlineRefreshButton`, `deferredRouteSsr`, `imperativeRefetch` → 70/70 pass.
- `type-check` (tsc --noEmit) → clean; `eslint` on `RSCProvider.tsx` → clean; `prettier --check` → clean.

body:
Non-control-plane correctness fix from the ultra-verify audit (Fedora-tool-usage P2).

## Gap
A monthly `--no-cache` base rebuild can land a **newer MariaDB on an existing `/var/lib/mysql` volume**, whose system tables then need `mariadb-upgrade`. The **grd** lineage gets this for free — `mariadb.service` runs `ExecStartPost=mariadb-check-upgrade`. The **xrdp** supervised-bash lineage backgrounds `mariadbd` directly with no equivalent, so a cross-version datadir could run un-upgraded (InnoDB redo-log recovery self-heals an unclean stop, but cross-version system-table upgrades are a separate step).

## Fix
Add an idempotent, **non-fatal** `mariadb-upgrade --socket=$DBSOCK` immediately after the readiness gate in `entrypoint.sh`:
- self-skips when the datadir is already current (keyed on `mysql_upgrade_info`),
- `|| true` ensures a failed/again-current run never blocks the desktop,
- tool name resolved with the same `mysql_*` fallback as the other MariaDB binaries.

xrdp-only; grd unaffected. Not control-plane.

## Description

The Payees page reports an inflated "associated rules" count. A payee with completed schedules shows a non-zero rule count, but clicking through to manage those rules shows nothing — because the rules being counted belong to schedules, not to the user.

Investigation traced the count through the data flow (frontend → API call → server function → in-memory rules) and found the defect server-side: `getPayeeRuleCounts()` in `packages/loot-core/src/server/payees/app.ts` iterates every rule with no filtering. Schedules auto-create rules in the same table as user-created rules, so each schedule silently inflates the number.

This change reuses the existing `getAllRuleIdsFromSchedules()` helper to build a `Set` of schedule-owned rule IDs and skips them while counting, so the count reflects only user-created rules — matching what the manage-rules screen actually lists.

AI disclosure: this change was written with Claude Code.

Closes #8134

Reproduced locally: created a schedule assigned to a payee, confirmed the Payees rule count incremented by 1, marked the schedule Completed, and confirmed the count did not drop. After the fix the count drops correctly and matches the manage-rules list.

```

After fix:   Payees page rule count = 0   →  Manage rules list shows 0 rules   (matches)
```

body: A joining fetch read the publisher forwarder's subscribers_ on relayExec_ while addChannelSubscriber wrote it on the publisher exec — an F14 data race. The read also never matched (the publisher forwarder keys channel subscribers by exec, not session), so LF joining fetches returned DOES_NOT_EXIST regardless. Resolve the join against the thread-local local forwarder on the subscriber exec before the relay hop (fetchOnSubscriberExec + LocalSubscribeFilter::fetch). Seed the subscribe-path subscriber's largest from the upstream OK so a post-SUBSCRIBE_OK joining fetch resolves; when it can't resolve yet (subscribe in progress, or pre-PUBLISH_OK), defer to upstream by track name. fetchImpl's joining block is now non-LF only. body: Re-syncs Paul Graham's blog (3 new essays → Vol V) **and** fixes the root cause of the directory-renumbering churn so future syncs stay clean. ## 1. New essays (→ Vol V) | Slug | Title | Date | Length | |------|-------|------|--------| | `brandage` | The Brand Age | Mar 2026 | ~25 pp | | `winc` | How to Convert Between Wealth and Income Tax | May 2026 | ~3 pp | | `earn` | How to Earn a Billion Dollars | Jun 2026 | ~8 pp | None removed upstream. All text-only (only `` tags are PG's nav/title GIFs, which the pipeline strips), so no new images. Generated LaTeX spot-checked: chapter titles, footnotes, and `\href` links all convert correctly and match existing conventions. ### Is Vol V too long now? → No The new essays land at the end of Vol V (where the `__last` cut already places everything after `disc`). | Volume | Pages | |--------|-------| | Vol I | 362 | | Vol II | 362 | | Vol III | 384 | | Vol IV | 381 | | **Vol V (before)** | **357** | | **Vol V (after)** | **391** | Vol V goes 357 → 391 (+34): the longest volume now, but only +7 over Vol III and well within print limits. Vol V was the shortest before; the set is now balanced (362–391). **No split needed.** ## 2. Fix: stable, append-only directory numbering **Root cause:** in `src/articleIndex.ts` the directory number came from each essay's position in PG's *newest-first* list, so every new post shifted every essay's number and renamed all dirs on each re-sync (a ~1,400-file churn). **Fix:** number dirs by *oldest-first* position (`000` = oldest). Because PG only prepends new essays, existing essays now keep their number forever and new posts simply get the next one — **no future re-sync renumbers existing dirs.** This PR also performs the one-time migration: all 231 dirs renamed to the new scheme. ## Phase 41 — Momentum / relative-strength board (`MOM`)

Ranks your **watchlist** by trailing returns across timeframes (type `MOM`, or `MOMENTUM` / `RS` / `STRENGTH`) — leaders float to the top, laggards to the bottom. A companion to the volatility dashboard (Phase 39).

### Per-symbol metrics (from daily candles)
| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **24H / 7D / 30D** | Trailing return over 1 / 7 / 30 daily bars |
| **RS** | Composite score — mean of the available look-backs |

author: flydyk
body:
## What

Person deep links now use a human-readable slug instead of the raw id.

- Before: `/person/p-0003`
- After: `/person/franciszek-kowalski-1788-p-0003`

The slug is `<given>-<surname>-<birthYear>-<id>` using the English name (falling back to a Cyrillic→Latin transliteration of `ru`/`be` when `en` is absent), with Latin diacritics folded to ASCII. The birth year is omitted when unknown.

## Why

The previous URL exposed an opaque internal id, so shared links gave no hint of who they pointed to. The slug makes links self-describing while staying stable.

## How it works

Resolution is **frontend-only** — the real id (`p-<digits>`) is appended verbatim as the slug's last segment and is the single source of truth. A regex (`extractPersonId`) recovers it, and the existing `GET /api/people/{id}` endpoint is unchanged. **No backend changes.**

Consequences that fall out of the design:
- **Backward compatible:** legacy `/person/p-0003` links still resolve (the bare id is a valid trailing-id match).
- **Self-healing:** the address bar `router.replace`s to the canonical slug once the person summary is loaded, so a cold bare-id deep link upgrades to the pretty form.
- **Robust:** the decorative name part can be truncated or stale and the link still resolves as long as the trailing id is intact.

## Changes

- `src/frontend/src/utils/personSlug.ts` (new) — pure `personSlug()` / `extractPersonId()` helpers (+ Vitest spec).
- `src/frontend/src/router/index.ts` — route param `:id` → `:slug`.
- `src/frontend/src/views/TreeView.vue` — derive the selected id from the slug, build slugs when navigating, and a canonicalization watcher that self-heals the URL.
- `docs/reference/` — routing/deep-link docs updated to the slug form.
- `docs/superpowers/` — design spec + implementation plan (historical).

## Testing

- `npm --prefix src/frontend test` — 748 passing, build (`vue-tsc`) clean.
- Verified live against the API (31 people): click → slug URL; legacy `/person/p-0005` → `/person/jozef-kowalski-1815-p-0005`; mangled `/person/whatever-name-here-p-0007` → `/person/wincenty-kowalski-1842-p-0007`. No console errors.

## Notes for reviewers

- Built via the superpowers brainstorm → spec → plan → subagent-driven flow; each task was reviewed, and a final whole-branch review passed (with the doc-sweep + minor tidies applied here).
- The two `TreeView.vue` watchers (panel-sync + canonicalization) share a `slugFor` helper and both guard on `route.params.slug !== slug`, so they converge without a navigation loop.

author: nothing-stops-this-train
body:
## Summary

Adds **payment receipts** to the CLINK offers flow and refreshes the project docs/licence.

When the server issues an invoice for a CLINK offer and that invoice later **settles**, the payer is now owed a follow-up `kind-21001` event whose decrypted body is `{"res":"ok"}` — byte-compatible with `@shocknet/clink-sdk`'s `NofferReceipt` (the payer's `onReceipt` callback). Previously nothing was sent after payment.

## How it works

- **`clink/receipts.py` (new)** — a pure, storage-backed `ReceiptRegistry` keyed by invoice payment hash, mirroring the `devfee`/`offers` style (injected `storage` mapping + clock, fully unit-testable with a plain dict). Lifecycle:
  - `remember()` on invoice issue → awaiting payment
  - `mark_due()` when paid → receipt owed, **persisted before any send** so a relay drop / Electrum restart can't lose it
  - `mark_sent()` on delivery → entry removed
  - bounded retry queue: redeliver owed receipts hourly and on every relay reconnect, sweep expired-unpaid entries, abandon after 10 days, cap the map at `MAX_PENDING`.
- **`clink/clink_plugin.py`** — delivers best-effort on settlement and from a periodic `_redeliver_receipts()` task; shares `_encrypt_event_args()` so the invoice and the receipt carry the same `["e", request_event_id]` tag the payer subscribes on. `liquidity_status()` now reports `owed_receipts`.
- **`clink/protocol.py`** — `receipt_payload()` centralises the `{"res":"ok"}` body.

## Tests

- 11 unit tests over the dict-backed registry (lifecycle, persistence across reload, idempotent `due`, expiry/abandon sweeps, retry throttling, cap eviction).
- A protocol shape test (`test_receipt_payload_is_sdk_shape`).
- An e2e test (`test_payment_receipt_delivered_after_payment`) asserting the payer receives the receipt after paying, via the regtest rig.

## Also in this PR (separate commit)

- **Docs:** README rewritten from marketing copy to developer docs (layout, configuration, CLI, tests, regtest-rig workflow, packaging).
- **Licence:** Unlicense → **MIT** (in both `LICENSE` and `pyproject.toml`).

> Note: the rolling-release workflow triggers on push to `main`, so it fires on merge, not on this branch.
